Guideline: Keep composables free of business logic
Description: Composables render state and emit events; data loading and business rules belong in a state holder such as a ViewModel
Do: Accept state and event lambdas as parameters
Don't: Call repositories or use cases from a composable
Code Bad: @Composable fun OrderRow(repository: OrderRepository) { val order = runBlocking { repository.load() } }

Guideline: Hoist state to make composables stateless
Description: Replace internal state with a value parameter and an event lambda so callers control it
Do: value: T plus onValueChange: (T) -> Unit
Don't: Hidden internal state in a component callers need to control
Code Bad: @Composable fun NameField() { var name by remember { mutableStateOf("") } ... }

Guideline: Expose one UI state per screen
Description: A screen's UI state comes from a single source, typically a StateFlow in the ViewModel
Do: Expose one immutable UiState stream
Don't: Several independently mutable flags read from different places
Code Bad: var isLoading = false; var error: String? = null // public and mutable

Guideline: Model UI state explicitly
Description: A sealed interface or data class makes every screen state representable and testable
Do: Sealed interface or data class for UI state
Don't: Combinations of boolean flags that allow impossible states
Code Good: sealed interface OrdersUiState { data object Loading : OrdersUiState; data class Ready(val orders: List<OrderUi>) : OrdersUiState }

Guideline: remember keeps state only across recomposition
Description: remember holds a value while the composable stays in the Composition; it is lost on configuration change
Do: remember for UI element state and expensive objects
Don't: remember for user input that must survive rotation
Code Bad: var draft by remember { mutableStateOf("") } // lost on rotation

Guideline: rememberSaveable for state that must survive recreation
Description: rememberSaveable saves Bundle-compatible values (or values with a Saver) across activity and process recreation
Do: rememberSaveable for user input and selection
Don't: remember for state the user expects to keep

Guideline: derivedStateOf when inputs change more often than the result
Description: derivedStateOf limits recomposition to changes in the derived value
Do: Wrap a frequently changing input whose derived result changes rarely
Don't: Read a per-frame value directly when only a threshold matters
Code Good: val showTop by remember { derivedStateOf { listState.firstVisibleItemIndex > 0 } }
Code Bad: val showTop = listState.firstVisibleItemIndex > 0 // recomposes while scrolling

Guideline: Key LaunchedEffect to the inputs it uses
Description: LaunchedEffect restarts when a key changes; Unit runs once for the composable's lifetime
Do: Pass every value whose change should restart the effect
Don't: LaunchedEffect(Unit) for work that depends on changing inputs
Code Bad: LaunchedEffect(Unit) { viewModel.load(userId) } // stale when userId changes

Guideline: rememberUpdatedState in long-lived effects
Description: A long-running effect that must call the latest lambda reads it through rememberUpdatedState instead of restarting
Do: rememberUpdatedState for callbacks used inside long-lived effects
Don't: Capture a lambda parameter directly in a long-lived effect
Code Good: val currentOnTimeout by rememberUpdatedState(onTimeout); LaunchedEffect(Unit) { delay(timeout); currentOnTimeout() }
Code Bad: LaunchedEffect(Unit) { delay(timeout); onTimeout() } // may call a stale lambda

Guideline: Clean up with DisposableEffect
Description: Effects that register listeners or observers must unregister them in onDispose
Do: DisposableEffect with an onDispose block
Don't: Register an observer from composition with no cleanup

Guideline: Unidirectional data flow
Description: State flows down and events flow up
Do: Pass state down and event lambdas up
Don't: Children writing to shared mutable state directly
Code Bad: Passing a MutableState into children that write to it

Guideline: Expose read-only state from the ViewModel
Description: Keep the mutable flow private and expose a read-only StateFlow
Do: Private MutableStateFlow with asStateFlow()
Don't: Public MutableStateFlow
Code Bad: val uiState = MutableStateFlow(UiState()) // anyone can write

Guideline: Collect flows with collectAsStateWithLifecycle
Description: On Android, collectAsStateWithLifecycle (lifecycle-runtime-compose) is the recommended way to collect flows; collectAsState suits platform-agnostic code
Do: collectAsStateWithLifecycle in Android UI
Don't: collectAsState in Android-only screens

Guideline: Reduce ViewModel-originated navigation to UI state
Description: Android guidance: ViewModel events should result in a UI state update. Channels and similar streams do not guarantee delivery when the ViewModel outlives the UI
Do: Expose the outcome (for example isUserLoggedIn) in UI state and let the UI call navigation
Don't: A Channel or SharedFlow of one-off navigation events from the ViewModel
Code Bad: private val events = Channel<NavEvent>(); val navEvents = events.receiveAsFlow()

Guideline: Use type-safe routes
Description: Navigation 2.8.0 and later define routes as @Serializable objects and classes
Do: @Serializable route types with composable<Route> and toRoute()
Don't: String routes with manually parsed arguments
Code Good: @Serializable data class Profile(val id: String) ... composable<Profile> { entry -> ProfileScreen(entry.toRoute<Profile>().id) }

Guideline: Rely on strong skipping; annotate stability only when it pays
Description: Strong skipping is on by default since Kotlin 2.0.20: unstable parameters compare by instance and lambdas are remembered. @Stable or @Immutable switches comparison to equals()
Do: Annotate only classes the compiler cannot infer (for example from non-Compose modules) whose equals is cheap and that are re-allocated with equal values
Don't: Blanket @Immutable on models holding large collections
Code Good: data class OrderUi(val id: String, val title: String) // inferred stable
Code Bad: @Immutable data class Feed(val items: List<Post>) // compares every element on each pass

Guideline: Provide stable keys in lazy lists
Description: Keys keep item state attached to the item when the list changes
Do: key = { it.id } in items()
Don't: Position-based identity for lists that reorder or insert

Guideline: Keep expensive work out of composition
Description: Composition can run often; cache derived values or compute them in the ViewModel
Do: remember with keys, or precompute in the state holder
Don't: Sort or filter large lists inside the composable body

Guideline: Read colors and type from MaterialTheme
Description: Material 3 color and typography roles keep components consistent across themes
Do: MaterialTheme.colorScheme and MaterialTheme.typography
Don't: Hard-coded color literals in composables

Guideline: Support dark theme through the color scheme
Description: Switch the whole color scheme with the system setting
Do: Provide light and dark color schemes
Don't: Fixed light colors regardless of theme
Code Good: MaterialTheme(colorScheme = if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) darkScheme else lightScheme) { App() }

Guideline: Prefer Modifier over extra layouts
Description: Use Modifier to adjust layout instead of adding wrapper composables
Do: Use Modifier.padding()
Don't: Wrap content with extra Box

Guideline: Avoid wrapper layouts that add no behavior
Description: Each layout adds measure and placement work; wrappers that only nest other layouts add cost without behavior
Do: Express spacing and alignment with Modifier, Arrangement, and Alignment
Don't: Box inside Column inside Box inside Row with no purpose

Guideline: Use Box for overlapping content
Description: Box stacks children; use Column or Row for sequential content
Do: Box for overlays and alignment within the same area
Don't: Box where children should flow vertically or horizontally
Code Bad: Box { Text(first); Text(second) } // meant to be a column

Guideline: Use lazy layouts for long or unbounded lists
Description: LazyColumn and LazyRow compose only visible items
Do: LazyColumn with keyed items
Don't: A scrollable Column that composes every item

Guideline: Do not nest scrollables in the same direction
Description: A LazyColumn inside a vertically scrolling parent receives an unbounded height constraint and fails
Do: One lazy list with header and footer items
Don't: LazyColumn inside Column.verticalScroll

Guideline: Use intrinsic measurements only when needed
Description: Intrinsic queries add a measurement pass; use them when a child must match a sibling's intrinsic size
Do: IntrinsicSize where siblings must share a size
Don't: IntrinsicSize on layouts by habit

Guideline: Use Arrangement and Alignment APIs
Description: Declare layout intent explicitly
Do: Use Arrangement / Alignment
Don't: Manual spacing hacks
Code Bad: A Spacer between every child to imitate arrangement

Guideline: Use the theme's typography
Description: Typography roles keep text consistent and scalable
Do: MaterialTheme.typography roles
Don't: Ad-hoc font sizes on individual Text calls

Guideline: Test stateless composables with semantics
Description: Stateless composables can be tested by passing state and asserting on semantics nodes
Do: setContent with explicit state and assert on what users perceive
Don't: Test composables that load their own data from the network
Code Bad: A test that waits on a real network call inside the composable

Guideline: Use testTag when no semantic match exists
Description: Prefer finders that match what users perceive; add a test tag when no stable semantic match exists
Do: onNodeWithText or onNodeWithContentDescription first; Modifier.testTag otherwise
Don't: Find nodes by fragile tree position

Guideline: Preview several states
Description: Previews of explicit states catch layout problems without running the app
Do: One @Preview per meaningful state, fed with sample state
Don't: A single preview that needs a live ViewModel

Guideline: Obtain ViewModels through Hilt
Description: Hilt constructs ViewModels with their dependencies; screens obtain them with hiltViewModel()
Do: @HiltViewModel with constructor injection
Don't: Construct ViewModels and their dependencies by hand in a composable
Code Good: @HiltViewModel class OrdersViewModel @Inject constructor(repository: OrdersRepository) : ViewModel() ... val viewModel: OrdersViewModel = hiltViewModel()
Code Bad: val viewModel = OrdersViewModel(OrdersRepository(api)) // inside a composable

Guideline: Describe meaningful images and icons
Description: Icon-only controls need a content description; decorative images use null
Do: contentDescription from string resources for meaningful icons
Don't: contentDescription = null on an icon-only button

Guideline: Give custom controls roles and labels
Description: Custom clickable elements need a role and an action label; related content can be merged into one node
Do: Modifier.clickable(role = Role.Button, onClickLabel = ...) and semantics(mergeDescendants = true)
Don't: A clickable Box with no role or label

Guideline: Use Compose animation APIs
Description: AnimatedVisibility and animate*AsState animate state changes declaratively
Do: AnimatedVisibility, animate*AsState, or updateTransition
Don't: A manual frame loop that updates state with delay()

Guideline: Keep animation state in the UI
Description: Animation is a UI concern driven by UI state
Do: Animate in composables from UI state
Don't: Emit animation progress values from the ViewModel

Guideline: Organize UI by feature module
Description: Feature modules keep screens and their dependencies separable
Do: Feature modules that depend on shared core modules
Don't: One module containing every screen

Guideline: Use observable state holders
Description: Non-observable mutable objects such as ArrayList do not trigger recomposition when they change
Do: mutableStateOf with immutable values, or mutableStateListOf
Don't: A remembered ArrayList mutated in place
Code Good: var items by remember { mutableStateOf(listOf<Item>()) }; items = items + newItem

Guideline: Pass new collection instances instead of mutating
Description: With strong skipping, unstable parameters such as List compare by instance, so an in-place mutation passes the same instance and readers can skip
Do: Emit a new list when contents change
Don't: Mutate a shared MutableList that composables receive

Guideline: rememberCoroutineScope for event-driven UI work
Description: Launch coroutines from callbacks with a scope that is cancelled when the composable leaves
Do: rememberCoroutineScope for UI work started by events
Don't: Use it for work that must outlive the screen (use viewModelScope)
Code Good: val scope = rememberCoroutineScope(); Button(onClick = { scope.launch { snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(message) } })
Code Bad: scope.launch { repository.sync() } // cancelled when the screen leaves

Guideline: Embed Views with AndroidView
Description: AndroidView hosts a View inside Compose; create it in factory and update it in update
Do: Create once in factory, apply state in update
Don't: Recreate the View on every recomposition
Code Good: AndroidView(factory = { context -> MapView(context) }, update = { view -> view.render(state) })
Code Bad: AndroidView(factory = { context -> MapView(context).also { it.render(state) } }) // state never updates

Guideline: Convert LiveData before reading it
Description: Compose recomposes from State; convert LiveData with observeAsState, and prefer StateFlow in new code
Do: observeAsState for LiveData; StateFlow with collectAsStateWithLifecycle in new code
Don't: Read liveData.value directly in a composable

Guideline: Measure recomposition before optimizing
Description: Layout Inspector shows recomposition and skip counts for composables
Do: Check recomposition counts while reproducing the slow interaction
Don't: Optimize without measuring
Code Good: Layout Inspector recomposition counts while scrolling the list
Code Bad: Adding remember and annotations by guesswork
